title: Shesha blueprint IR (machine twin)
description:
The JSON twin of a screen blueprint. Comprehension emits it alongside the Markdown blueprint (fenced blueprint-json block); shesha-form-edit's compile-blueprint.js validates against this schema and refuses to compile a blueprint that does not satisfy it. This file is a VALIDATOR, not a prompt — the authoring guidance for the node grammar lives in shesha-form-edit/references/designing-like-react.md.

DESIGN INTENT IS PART OF THE IR. A blueprint states hierarchy (`emphasis`), surface (`surface`), information density (`density`), number and date presentation (`format`), and the designed empty state (`emptyState`). The compiler resolves each of these to concrete component channels using the brand token file — so the SAME blueprint renders on-brand for any theme, and nothing about the visual outcome is left for a later pass to invent. Every slot here maps to a channel the component KB records for the target component; there is no decorative key that the compiler silently drops.

fullClassName.description: resolved entity type string, as dataContext.entityType takes it

modelType.description: formSettings.modelType [R-016]. BOTH keys are required — a half-resolved modelType is the portability defect that makes a form bind on one backend and silently fail on another.

archetype.description: golden archetype key — must exist in shesha-form-edit/assets/golden/_index.json

theme.description: brand token file name (e.g. 'shesha'); resolved to a style plan at compile time

fidelity.description: A readable source · B runnable probe · C screenshot/vision

viewport.description: the ONE viewport used for both capture and verification

density.description: screen-wide default density. Nodes inherit it unless they set their own. Omitted, the archetype's default applies (worklists compact, capture/detail default).

bindings.description: Per-property presentation for FIELD nodes. Datatable columns do NOT read this — a column carries its own label/component/format inline, so there is no second list to keep in agreement.

component.description: explicit component type; omit for by-datatype selection

assertions.description: placement contract re-measured after build — membership, grouping, nesting depth, tab key; never pixels

propertyPath.description: camelCase entity property, or a dotted nav path. PascalCase renders blank cells [R-004/R-034].

width.description: flex-child width — %, px, fr or calc(); compiled to desktop.dimensions.width, the only split lever [R-028]

spacing.description: px number or scale token xs|sm|md|lg|xl|2xl

emphasis.description:
Where this element sits in the reading order — the schema slot for the design standard 'one element is clearly most important per view'.

identity = the value that names the record (a reference, a person's name); rendered at the strong ink and weight.
primary  = the single focal point of the view. Validation FAILS a screen with two `primary` siblings in the same region, because two focal points is none.
secondary = normal reading weight; the default when omitted.
muted    = supporting metadata, de-emphasised ink.

Resolved to desktop.font.{size,weight,color} from the brand type scale and ink roles — never to a hard-coded hex.

tone.description: ink role for non-structural text, resolved to roles.{bodyText,secondaryText,mutedText,helperText}. Use `emphasis` for hierarchy and `tone` only to pick a shade within it.

density.description: Information density — the schema slot for 'density matches the audience'. On a datatable it resolves to rowPadding* and rowDimensions; on a layout node to gap and padding. compact = operational worklists that enumerate; comfortable = executive summaries that aggregate.

surface.description: What this container reads as, resolved from the brand roles: canvas = the muted page background (roles.pageBg) · card = white panel with the brand hairline, plus the brand card shadow only if the brand defines one (roles.cardBg) · sunken = inset/read-only surface (roles.readOnlyFieldBg) · none = no background, pure layout. Supports the standard that most of a page is NOT white.

format.description:
How a bound value is PRESENTED. Resolved to the display component's real channels — `dataType` (string|date-time|number|boolean), `numberFormat` (currency|double|round|thousandSeparator) and `dateFormat`. Discriminated on `kind`, so a date pattern on a number is a validation error rather than a silently ignored key.

This def deliberately carries NOTHING the runtime cannot honour. In particular there is no currency `code` and no `unit`: the framework's formatter hard-codes en-ZA/ZAR (utils/string.ts), and no unit channel exists — so a unit belongs in the column LABEL ('Total (ZAR)'), which is also how the standards' 'every number carries a unit' is meant to be satisfied. There is no `percent` kind for the same reason.

kind.description: → numberFormat 'currency'. Rendered in ZAR by the framework formatter; state a different currency in the label.

decimals.description: 0 → 'round', 2 → 'double'-style two-decimal money. The formatter offers no other precision.

thousands.description: true → 'thousandSeparator'. Mutually exclusive with `decimals` — the formatter applies one numberFormat, not both.

pattern.description: day.js pattern → dateFormat; default DD MMM YYYY
day.js pattern → dateFormat; default DD MMM YYYY HH:mm

transform.description: emitted via the `style` code-mode channel — the measured way to reach textTransform, which the font channel cannot express

truncate.description: → ellipsis. A line COUNT is not available; the runtime truncates to one line.

emptyState.description: The designed no-data state. The standards call a bare default 'No Data' a failure of the bar, and this is the slot that lets a blueprint say otherwise. Resolved to noDataText / noDataSecondaryText / noDataIcon.

body.description: one line telling the user what to do about it

column.description: One datatable column. A bare string is shorthand for { property } — use the object form to state label, component, alignment and number format, so nothing about the column is left to be inferred after the blueprint.

label.description: column caption. Omitted, the compiler title-cases the property, which is usually NOT what a reader wants ('bookingReference' → 'Booking Reference' rather than 'Reference').

component.description: cell component type for a non-default rendering, e.g. refListStatus for a status chip. Compiled to the column's displayComponent with a full migrated settings model.

align.description: cell + header alignment. Numbers belong right-aligned per the standards; the compiler defaults numeric formats to right and warns when a currency/number column is explicitly left-aligned.

width.description: fixed px width; sets minWidth = maxWidth so the column does not breathe

description.description: header tooltip; the place to expand an abbreviation on first use

rowAction.description: What clicking a row does. Compiled to onRowClick (or onRowDoubleClick when trigger is doubleClick). Omit for a read-only table — but on a worklist whose rows have a detail view, omitting it is the most common reason a built screen feels unfinished.

type.description: navigate = go to a form/url · dialog = open a modal form

module.description: target form module; defaults to this form's module

url.description: type=navigate with a raw url instead of a form

toolbarAction.description: One toolbar button. The compiler always emits quick search and a pager for a table; these are the SEMANTIC actions on top of that chrome.

emphasis.description: at most ONE toolbar action may be `primary` — the brand-filled button. The rest render as default white buttons, per 'colour is an accent, never a surface'.

node.description: One layout node, discriminated on `kind`. Each kind carries only the properties that mean something for it, so a width on a field or columns on a card is a validation error rather than a silently ignored key.

container.description: alias of stack, kept for blueprints already in flight

row.description: horizontal flex. Children are sized with `width`; a row is the ONLY way to split, never the columns component [R-028].

surface.description: defaults to `card` — a card node that sets surface:none is a layout group and should probably be a stack

section.description: titled group. The title is the point — an untitled group is a stack.

grid.description: equal-width columns. `columns` is a COUNT here — contrast datatable, where it is a list of bound properties.

tabs.description: children may ONLY be tab nodes — a tab is meaningless anywhere else, so it is not part of the general node union.

key.description: stable tab key; assertions reference it

component.description: explicit component type override; omit for by-datatype selection

readOnly.description: render as a read-only value rather than an input

truncate.description: → ellipsis. The runtime truncates to one line; there is no line-count channel.

level.description: 1 page title … 4 label. Drives the type scale, so it is required — an unsized heading renders at body size and the page loses hierarchy.

datatable.description: `columns` is the list of BOUND PROPERTIES to show, not a count. The compiler always wraps it in a dataContext and emits quick search + a pager; `toolbar` and `rowAction` add the screen's semantic actions on top.

striped.description: zebra rows. Defaults false — rowDividers carry row separation per the standards, and stripes on top of dividers reads as noise.

datalist.description: repeats an item form per record. Use for card lists; use datatable for anything a reader will scan in columns.

itemModule.description: item form module; defaults to this form's module

chip.description: A status pill. Compiles to refListStatus — there is no `chip` component in the runtime, so the reference-list item supplies the colour and the word together [R-036]. Colour alone never conveys status.

property.description: the reference-list status property; the chip colour comes from the reflist item [R-036]

showLabel.description: prefix the reference list's own name; usually noise on a card

actions.description: The action row. `exit` is REQUIRED and explicit: a Submit with no way out leaves a form the user can save but not leave [R-007], and the correct exit depends on how the screen is presented — the compiler cannot infer it.

submit.description: the forward action; omit to accept the default Save/Submit

type.description: back = standalone page (Navigate) · close-dialog = modal · cancel-edit = detail view in edit mode
